listeningSets.transcript: The student volunteer office is organizing reading visits to a nearby primary school. A Saturday team reached its maximum size. The new group will meet on Sunday afternoon. Applications close before Thursday noon. Volunteers should bring a student card and one picture book. No teaching experience is needed because mentors will give a short orientation. Students who miss orientation can watch the recorded briefing. The organizers explained that the arrangement would be reviewed after participants had shared practical feedback. Clear instructions were published in advance so that beginners could prepare without unnecessary pressure. Staff members recorded attendance and common questions to improve the next stage of campus volunteering. Participants were encouraged to ask for help whenever a detail of the plan seemed unclear. The team also considered accessibility, cost, travel time, and the needs of students with busy schedules. A short follow-up survey would compare expectations with the experience reported after the activity.

segments.text: The student volunteer office is organizing reading visits to a nearby primary school.
A Saturday team reached its maximum size. The new group will meet on Sunday afternoon.
Applications close before Thursday noon. Volunteers should bring a student card and one picture book.
No teaching experience is needed because mentors will give a short orientation.
Students who miss orientation can watch the recorded briefing.
The organizers explained that the arrangement would be reviewed after participants had shared practical feedback.
Clear instructions were published in advance so that beginners could prepare without unnecessary pressure.
Staff members recorded attendance and common questions to improve the next stage of campus volunteering.
Participants were encouraged to ask for help whenever a detail of the plan seemed unclear.
The team also considered accessibility, cost, travel time, and the needs of students with busy schedules.
A short follow-up survey would compare expectations with the experience reported after the activity.

questions.prompt: After the original campus volunteering plan became unavailable, which alternative time did the notice announce?
options: The new group will meet on Sunday afternoon.
Individual consultations are available on Monday evening.
The launch event is Saturday morning beside the central café.
The coach departs at eight on Sunday morning.
questions.explanationZh: 原文依据：The new group will meet on Sunday afternoon.

questions.prompt: What situation led organizers to schedule the event described as “The new group will meet on Sunday afternoon.”?
options: Many students requested help after the daytime desks closed.
A Saturday team reached its maximum size.
Disposable cup waste rose sharply last semester.
Saturday was avoided because several departments hold tests then.
questions.explanationZh: 原文依据：A Saturday team reached its maximum size.

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarizes the notice that begins “The student volunteer office is organizing reading visits to a nearby primary school.”?
options: The library has launched appointments for its research-support desk.
An environmental group is starting a reusable-cup campaign in campus cafés.
The student volunteer office is organizing reading visits to a nearby primary school.
The international office is arranging a low-cost weekend trip to a historic town.
questions.explanationZh: 原文依据：The student volunteer office is organizing reading visits to a nearby primary school.

questions.prompt: By what point must a listener act before following the plan “The new group will meet on Sunday afternoon.”?
options: Bookings must be made by Friday at six.
Volunteers should register by Thursday.
Payment and registration are due by Tuesday.
Applications close before Thursday noon.
questions.explanationZh: 原文依据：Applications close before Thursday noon.

questions.prompt: Which preparation matches the notice after the deadline “Applications close before Thursday noon.”?
options: Volunteers should bring a student card and one picture book.
Visitors need a library card and a draft search question.
They need comfortable shoes and a refillable bottle.
Travelers need an identity card and packed lunch.
questions.explanationZh: 原文依据：Volunteers should bring a student card and one picture book.

questions.prompt: What can a first-time participant infer from the statement “No teaching experience is needed because mentors will give a short orientation.”?
options: First-year students are welcome and do not need database experience.
No teaching experience is needed because mentors will give a short orientation.
Campaign training will be provided at the start.
A guide will explain the sites in both Chinese and English.
questions.explanationZh: 原文依据：No teaching experience is needed because mentors will give a short orientation.

questions.prompt: What alternative is available if the main arrangement for campus volunteering cannot be followed?
options: A librarian will answer remaining questions by email.
Rain will move the activity into the student center.
Students who miss orientation can watch the recorded briefing.
The fee will be refunded if severe weather cancels the trip.
questions.explanationZh: 原文给出的替代安排是：Students who miss orientation can watch the recorded briefing.

questions.prompt: By offering “Students who miss orientation can watch the recorded briefing.”, what attitude do the organizers show toward possible difficulties?
options: They dismiss every concern raised about campus volunteering.
They insist that no plan connected with campus volunteering can change.
They are flexible and willing to help participants.
They blame participants before the campus volunteering activity begins.
questions.explanationZh: 原文提供替代安排，体现组织者愿意灵活解决困难：Students who miss orientation can watch the recorded briefing.

questions.prompt: Which pair of actions would best prepare a student for the campus volunteering arrangement?
options: Bookings must be made by Friday at six. Visitors need a library card and a draft search question.
Volunteers should register by Thursday. They need comfortable shoes and a refillable bottle.
Payment and registration are due by Tuesday. Travelers need an identity card and packed lunch.
Applications close before Thursday noon. Volunteers should bring a student card and one picture book.
questions.explanationZh: 应同时注意截止时间和准备事项：Applications close before Thursday noon. Volunteers should bring a student card and one picture book.

questions.prompt: What does the message imply about students with little previous experience in campus volunteering?
options: They can participate because guidance or support is available.
They are automatically refused a place.
They must organize the entire activity alone.
They may join only after completing a university degree.
questions.explanationZh: 原文说明会提供支持，因此缺少经验并不会阻止参加：No teaching experience is needed because mentors will give a short orientation.

questions.prompt: Considering the statement “The student volunteer office is organizing reading visits to a nearby primary school.”, which conclusion is supported by the complete campus volunteering message?
options: The announced detail should be understood together with the other instructions.
The statement proves that every other instruction can be ignored.
The statement describes an unrelated commercial advertisement.
The message asks listeners to invent a different event.

Participants repeatedly identified regular peer check-ins as the feature that made progress easier to maintain. Many participants said that regular peer check-ins removed a practical obstacle. writingPrompts.prompt: Your university is collecting suggestions for encouraging daily reading. Write an essay explaining why the habit matters and propose one workable activity. Write 120–180 words.
outline: Explain the value of daily reading
Describe one realistic campus reading activity
Show how students could maintain the habit
writingPrompts.referenceOpening: A daily reading habit gives students a reliable way to widen their knowledge and sharpen their thinking.
writingPrompts.referenceAnswer: A daily reading habit gives students a reliable way to widen their knowledge and sharpen their thinking. Reading for only twenty minutes a day can improve vocabulary, concentration, and the ability to compare different ideas. The university could therefore hold a month-long reading relay. Each participant would choose an accessible book, record one useful sentence after every session, and share a short comment with a small group each Friday. The activity should reward steady participation instead of the number of pages finished, so beginners would not feel pressured. Librarians could prepare themed book lists and quiet reading corners. After the relay, students could keep the same daily time slot and exchange books with their partners. In this way, a temporary campus activity could gradually become a personal habit that supports every subject.

writingPrompts.prompt: Write an essay for the campus newspaper describing what students can learn from volunteer work. Support your view with an example. Write 120–180 words.
outline: State what volunteer work can teach
Connect the lesson to future study or work
writingPrompts.referenceOpening: Volunteer work teaches lessons that are difficult to learn from textbooks alone.
writingPrompts.referenceAnswer: Volunteer work teaches lessons that are difficult to learn from textbooks alone. When students serve real people, they learn to listen carefully, solve unexpected problems, and take responsibility for a result. For instance, a volunteer helping older residents use mobile services may discover that clear instructions require patience rather than technical language. The student must notice confusion, explain one step at a time, and protect private information. Such experience develops communication and empathy, while also showing where one's own knowledge is incomplete. A useful volunteer program should include brief training and a reflection meeting after each visit. Students can then connect the difficulties they met with lessons from class. These practical habits will remain valuable in future teamwork, customer service, and community life.

writingPrompts.prompt: Many students struggle to balance study and rest. Write an essay explaining how effective time management can help and recommend a practical method. Write 120–180 words.
outline: Describe the result of using it consistently
writingPrompts.referenceOpening: Managing time well does not mean filling every minute; it means protecting time for both study and rest.
writingPrompts.referenceAnswer: Managing time well does not mean filling every minute; it means protecting time for both study and rest. A simple method is to divide the day into three blocks: focused study, necessary tasks, and genuine rest. At the beginning of each week, a student can choose two important goals and place fixed study sessions on a calendar. Smaller jobs should fill the spaces around them instead of replacing them. During a study block, the phone can stay outside reach; when the block ends, taking a walk or talking with friends becomes planned recovery rather than guilty delay. The schedule should also leave one open period for unexpected work. After reviewing the plan each evening, students can adjust the next day. Consistent use of this method reduces last-minute pressure and makes both learning and rest more satisfying.

writingPrompts.prompt: Write an essay discussing one healthy habit that college students often overlook and explain how the university could encourage it. Write 120–180 words.
writingPrompts.referenceOpening: Among the habits college students overlook, regular sleep is one of the most important.
writingPrompts.referenceAnswer: Among the habits college students overlook, regular sleep is one of the most important. Many students stay awake to finish assignments or use their phones, then depend on coffee the next morning. This pattern weakens attention, memory, and emotional control, so the extra waking hours often produce poor work. Universities can help by running a two-week sleep challenge rather than giving another general lecture. Participants could set a regular bedtime, record screen-free minutes before sleep, and compare their daytime energy privately. Residence halls might dim common-area lights late at night, while libraries could publicize earlier planning services during busy weeks. The goal is not to control students but to make healthy choices easier. Better sleep would improve classroom participation and reduce the need for exhausting last-minute study.

writingPrompts.prompt: Online learning offers flexibility but also creates difficulties. Write an essay evaluating both sides and state how students should use it. Write 120–180 words.
outline: Set out rules for responsible use
writingPrompts.referenceOpening: Online learning is most useful when flexibility is balanced with self-discipline.
writingPrompts.referenceAnswer: Online learning is most useful when flexibility is balanced with self-discipline. Recorded lessons allow students to review difficult points and learn when travel or illness prevents attendance. However, the same screen also carries messages, games, and endless links, while delayed viewing can quickly create a backlog. Students should treat an online course like a real appointment. Before each session, they can close unrelated tabs, write one question to answer, and set a finishing time. Watching should be followed by a short summary or practice task, because passive replay creates an illusion of understanding. A weekly checklist can reveal unfinished lessons before they become overwhelming. Teachers should provide clear deadlines and brief discussion opportunities. With these limits, flexibility supports learning instead of turning into postponement.

writingPrompts.prompt: A student club wants to improve teamwork. Write an essay identifying a common team problem and suggesting how members can solve it. Write 120–180 words.
outline: Explain its effect on the group
writingPrompts.referenceOpening: Effective teamwork begins when members understand both their shared goal and their individual responsibility.
writingPrompts.referenceAnswer: Effective teamwork begins when members understand both their shared goal and their individual responsibility. A common team problem is silent disagreement about who should do what. Active members become overloaded, quieter members wait for instructions, and the final work lacks a consistent direction. The group should begin by turning its goal into small tasks with named owners and visible deadlines. A shared page can record decisions, but a ten-minute weekly meeting is still needed to report obstacles and ask for help. The team leader should invite each member to speak and should change assignments when one person is carrying too much. At the end, members can review which process worked rather than only celebrating the product. Clear responsibility and regular communication make cooperation fairer and help everyone contribute useful strengths.

writingPrompts.prompt: Write an essay persuading students to take one realistic environmental action on campus and explain its possible impact. Write 120–180 words.
writingPrompts.referenceOpening: A greener campus can begin with one realistic action repeated by many students.
writingPrompts.referenceAnswer: A greener campus can begin with one realistic action repeated by many students. Reducing disposable cups is achievable because students make the same purchase many times each week. Campus cafés could offer a small discount to customers who bring a reusable cup and lend returnable cups to those who forget. Clear washing stations and return points would remove the main inconvenience. Student volunteers could publish the number of cups avoided each month, allowing participants to see the combined effect of ordinary choices. The campaign should begin with two busy cafés, collect feedback, and expand only after the system works smoothly. Visible results would encourage more people than moral slogans alone. If the habit spreads, the university would reduce waste, lower purchasing costs, and show that environmental action can be practical.

writingPrompts.prompt: Your university plans to redesign campus activities. Write an essay describing which kind of activity deserves more support and why. Write 120–180 words.
outline: Name the activity that deserves support
Explain the skills or connections it develops
Recommend how the university should organize it
writingPrompts.referenceOpening: Campus activities deserve support when they help students build skills and genuine connections.
writingPrompts.referenceAnswer: Campus activities deserve support when they help students build skills and genuine connections. Collaborative workshops deserve more support than activities in which students only sit and watch. A workshop on public speaking, photography, or cultural storytelling asks participants to create something together, exchange feedback, and meet people outside their usual classes. The university could offer small rooms, basic equipment, and trained student hosts while keeping each group below twenty members. Every meeting should end with a modest product, such as a short presentation or photo story, so progress is visible. Beginners could join an introductory session before choosing a longer project. This structure would produce genuine connections and useful skills without demanding a large budget. Campus life would become a place for participation rather than a calendar of passive events.

writingPrompts.prompt: Write an essay explaining why career planning should begin before graduation and identify the first step a student can take. Write 120–180 words.
outline: Describe how that step supports a later decision
writingPrompts.referenceOpening: Career planning should start before graduation because useful experience takes time to develop.
writingPrompts.referenceAnswer: Career planning should start before graduation because useful experience takes time to develop. The first step is not choosing a permanent job title but learning what kinds of work match one's interests and abilities. A student can select three possible fields, read real job descriptions, and note the skills that appear repeatedly. The next step is to interview an older student or professional and ask what daily work actually involves. This information can guide the choice of a course, internship, or campus project during the following semester. Keeping a short record of completed tasks and feedback will also make future résumés more specific. Early exploration leaves time to change direction without panic. By graduation, students who have tested several options can make decisions based on evidence instead of fashion or family pressure.

writingPrompts.prompt: Digital tools can either support or interrupt study. Write an essay explaining how students can use them more responsibly. Write 120–180 words.
outline: Propose clear limits for responsible use
writingPrompts.referenceOpening: Digital tools improve learning only when students control how and when they use them.
writingPrompts.referenceAnswer: Digital tools improve learning only when students control how and when they use them. Calendar applications, online dictionaries, and note systems can save time and make learning materials easier to find. The danger begins when every alert interrupts attention or when students collect resources without using them. A responsible rule is to assign each tool one clear purpose. Notifications should be turned off during focused work, entertainment applications can have daily limits, and important files should follow a simple naming system. Students might also check messages at fixed times instead of reacting immediately. Once a week, they should remove unused applications and review whether a tool improved an actual result. Technology should reduce decisions and support practice; if it creates more distraction than value, the simplest solution may be to stop using it.

writingPrompts.prompt: Write an essay about one improvement you would make to public transport around your university and explain who would benefit. Write 120–180 words.
writingPrompts.referenceOpening: Reliable public transport around a university benefits students, staff, and nearby residents alike.
writingPrompts.referenceAnswer: Reliable public transport around a university benefits students, staff, and nearby residents alike. Around many campuses, buses become crowded at class-changing times but arrive too rarely in the evening. The university and city could test a later circular route linking the main gate, residence halls, railway station, and nearby neighborhoods. A mobile timetable should show real arrival times, while the final two services should wait for evening classes to end. During a one-month trial, passenger counts and short surveys could identify which stops are truly needed. Students would gain a safer trip home, staff could work flexible hours, and residents would reach university facilities without driving. If the data show steady demand, the route could become permanent and reduce both traffic pressure and unnecessary private-car journeys.

writingPrompts.prompt: Your class will hold an international cultural exchange event. Write an essay proposing an activity and explaining how it promotes understanding. Write 120–180 words.
outline: Explain how participants would take part
Show how it could deepen mutual understanding
writingPrompts.referenceOpening: A well-designed cultural exchange activity allows participants to learn with one another rather than simply watch a performance.
writingPrompts.referenceAnswer: A well-designed cultural exchange activity allows participants to learn with one another rather than simply watch a performance. The university could organize a culture studio in which small mixed groups learn one another's everyday traditions through a shared task. Instead of watching formal performances, participants might cook a simple festival food, explain the story behind an object, or create a bilingual guide to a local custom. Before the event, each group would prepare questions and agree not to treat one person as the representative of an entire culture. Student hosts could help with language difficulties and make sure everyone contributes. At the end, groups would present what surprised them and correct one earlier assumption. Working together makes differences concrete but not threatening. Such exchange can build curiosity, respectful communication, and friendships that continue after the activity.
